content: The game was incredibly fun on first release, it ended up getting stale due to lack of events, flash forwards 10 years later and there is an abundance of quests and events to do so that you don’t ever have to spend a penny on the game. With that being said though you will almost never get the main banner characters unless you put actual money into the game. I’ve saved 600 stones to not pull a single banner lead for an event. I spent $40 on the next event and voila I magically got the main banner card in 3-5 summons. Game is great but the obvious gotcha mechanics will prevent many new players from wanting to continue to play once they get all caught up and realize they can no longer do any event without the newest banner card, which will then lead to waiting 4-6 months for the carnival or other festival banner to get the units that were good 6 months ago and waiting for the current unit to become old, the forever rinse and repeat cycle.

author: Chcuk Norris
title: Fun game, difficult to get into.
content:
As the title implies, the game is really hard to get into, but really fun once you know what you’re doing. 

The units and their special attack animations are phenomenal and pretty much 1-1 with the show. 
There is a certain synergy between some of the units which provides an excellent team building system.

But, In the beginning it’s kinda difficult to play. Don’t get me wrong, building up a team is satisfying, but only with the right cards. You summon for your units through dragon stones, which you can purchase or the Admins give out doing holidays or events. The easiest time to really play are during the anniversary’s, the 7th one just passed as of writing this. The devs pump out a ton of dragon stones and have really good units to boot. But playing anytime after, it’s pretty empty. The Global version (the version you and I are currently playing on) don’t get the cool new units the JP (Japanese Version) gets. So it’s usually cool unit drops, a banner with lesser units in between, then another cool unit.

It also won’t help certain units that need a small boost, but not an eza boost. Example: Super Saiyan god ss Vegeta (agl version from tournament of power) has a 30% chance to awaken after turn four, but a unit like super saiyan broly (phy from movie) just awakes after turn four. I’d be OK with this if Vegeta’s awakening was better than broly’s, but it’s not. They really should buff the awakenings on older characters to match that of newer ones, because some characters just never awaken, like LR int Super saiyan goku and vegeta. title: This game is better than Dragon ball legends
content:
I am going to write a whole essay on why this game is better than legends
Dragon Ball Z Dokkan Battle is a mobile game based on the Dragon Ball Z anime series that offers players a unique and exciting experience. It is regarded as one of the best mobile games of all time and has become a worldwide sensation across multiple platforms.

In comparison, "Dragon Ball Legends" is another mobile game that shares similar characteristics to "Dragon Ball Z Dokkan Battle", but it falls short in terms of gameplay mechanics, characters, and overall quality.

One of the main reasons why "Dragon Ball Z Dokkan Battle" is considered superior is because of its diverse and complex gameplay. It offers players a wide range of characters, including some of the most powerful and iconic characters from the Dragon Ball Z series, each with their own unique abilities and strengths. This adds a layer of depth to the gameplay mechanics, making it more engaging and rewarding for players. Additionally, the game features a variety of challenging events and missions, which offer unique rewards upon completion, incentivizing players to keep coming back for more.

In contrast, "Dragon Ball Legends" lacks this depth in its gameplay mechanics. The characters are less interesting, and the gameplay can become repetitive and mundane over time. The game also features fewer events and missions compared to "Dragon Ball Z Dokkan Battle", which further limits its replayability. Additionally, "Dragon Ball Legends" lacks the iconic characters and moments from the Dragon Ball Z series, making it less engaging for fans of the franchise.

Furthermore, "Dragon Ball Z Dokkan Battle" is known for its generous rewards system, allowing players to earn free dragon stones and other valuable items through gameplay. This motivates players to keep playing and gives them a sense of progress and achievement. "Dragon Ball Legends", on the other hand, limits the number of resources players can earn, making it more difficult to progress in the game without spending money.

In conclusion, "Dragon Ball Z Dokkan Battle" is the better game overall, thanks to its more engaging gameplay mechanics, diverse character roster, and generous rewards system. "Dragon Ball Legends", while still a solid mobile game, falls short in these areas, making it less appealing to both die-hard Dragon Ball Z fans and casual gamers.

author: Seventh Dragon Ball Fan
title: Very good (if your a dragon ball fan)
content: I think the game is really fun when you look at the level of design put into the modern cards. Post 10th anniversary, the new standard is outright surpassing the anime in terms of animation and making the scenes from the anime look so much better. My gripes with the game is the gameplay that is sometimes entirely rng based, so when you lose, it’s less likely that you have a bad team and more likely that you just got unlucky stats that you didn’t build up so you ended up doing less damage and it costed you the game, or you got unlucky after failing a 70 percent dodge rate. Plus, if you do have a bad team, there’s no way to just get a better team because this is a gacha, so as a free to play player who has a team that is out of the meta, all they can really do is farm dragon stones to just get shafted again again and again. Also I really hate the categories in this game I don’t see the point in it if most of the categories don’t even fit the character or are just entirely void in characters that should have them.
